title: Sum an Array
prompt: A dashboard receives a list of daily point totals. Write a function that returns the sum of all numbers in the array. If there are no entries yet, return 0.

explanation.beginner:
Example: sumArray([1,2,3]) produces 6. Keep a running sum initialized to zero. Each element contributes once; the empty list contributes nothing.

Compare “sums to zero for an empty list”: input [[]] produces 0. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Keep a running sum initialized to zero. Each element contributes once; the empty list contributes nothing.

Tempting mistake: Starting from the first element without an empty-list guard can produce undefined or throw.

The reference uses reduce. Trace the intermediate value after each operation; count repeated scans inside callbacks separately when estimating cost. One pass costs O(n) time and O(1) accumulator space.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “sums to zero for an empty list”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
